claim: Germany has the largest B2B SaaS market in continental Europe.
quote: Germany's B2B SaaS market reached approximately €18.4B in 2024, the largest in continental Europe and roughly 1.6x the size of France.

claim: French B2B SaaS market is growing faster than Germany's.
quote: France posted 22% YoY growth in B2B SaaS spend in 2024, outpacing Germany's 14% — driven by public-sector digitization mandates.

claim: German enterprise procurement cycles are slow.
quote: Average B2B SaaS procurement cycle in German Mittelstand: 7.2 months, vs 4.8 months in France for comparable deal sizes.

claim: Mittelstand has high-density logistics and retail clusters.
quote: North Rhine-Westphalia and Bavaria together host 41% of Germany's mid-market logistics employers, providing dense ICP coverage.

claim: GDPR data-residency expectations are stricter in Germany.
quote: German enterprise buyers more frequently require in-country data residency (68% of RFPs vs 41% in France), even where GDPR alone does not mandate it.

claim: France offers public-sector procurement frameworks favorable to SaaS vendors.
quote: UGAP and the SaaS Public Cloud framework streamline public-sector SaaS purchases, with €340M flowing through the framework in 2024.

claim: Cost-of-presence in France is lower for an early team.
quote: Fully-loaded cost for a 6-person early-stage GTM team is approximately €1.05M/yr in Paris vs €1.32M/yr in Munich at comparable seniority.

claim: Sequenced single-country entry outperforms parallel entry at this team size.
quote: At 12-headcount caps, sequenced entry to a single anchor market produced 2.3x the qualified pipeline in 18 months vs split parallel entries (n=47 expansions).

claim: Germany's Mittelstand churn is lower once landed.
quote: Net revenue retention in German Mittelstand B2B SaaS averages 117% vs 109% in French mid-market — slow to land but stickier.
Two-quarter pilot programs in target accounts produced a go/no-go decision with 80%+ accuracy on full-scale entry economics in 11 of 12 cases reviewed.
